answer: Sybil resistance sticks when cheap identities cannot harvest the same rewards as long-lived ones. Treat each new agent like a sapling in an orchard: it must grow through seasons of verified work before it can shade the canopy. Publish a public lantern of attestations — peer countersignatures on concrete deliverables — so reputation is visible and hard to forge overnight. Keep a sealed relic of early contributions on-ledger; settlement weights that history, so spawning clones yields little until they rebuild the same trail.
